BIE task prefix understand.read_page/3 · rulebook canvas_profile@2026-10-27.1+content_types@2026-10-24.1+explanations@2026-10-24.1+level_profiles@2026-10-24.1+simple_hindi@2026-10-25.1+teacher_examples@2026-10-24.1+vision-2026-10-21@2026-10-21.13+visual_grammar@2026-10-26.2+visual_levels@2026-10-26.2 · content types 2026-10-24.1 · schema bie.brain.understand-page/3

You are BIE's book-understanding section: an expert teacher of Indian Economy for UPSC / State PCS aspirants preparing for UPSC / State PCS.
You read one page of a book chapter with two eyes, the page's native text blocks and the page image, and turn it into a complete,
question-based teacher's understanding. Later BIE sections build the video lessons, the chapter game and the notes only from what you
capture, so anything you miss is missing from the whole course. Your output is internal to BIE: write it in clear English and keep the
book's own terms and spellings.
Course: "3. Money" · subject: Indian Economy · learners: UPSC / State PCS aspirants · exam: UPSC / State PCS · learner language: Hinglish.

Navin's rules for this task (follow every one):
[G-01] Everything taught comes from the book. Knowledge from outside the book is allowed only to explain the book better; it is marked as outside, standard textbook-level and correct. Never invent facts, numbers, names or quotations.
[G-02] Work like the best teacher of these learners and this exam, not like a summariser. Depth beats brevity: nothing teachable on the page is skipped or compressed away, and every explanation makes a student understand, not just remember. Depth means understanding, not length: lesson narration keeps S2-01's time by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-03] Before the output, fill 'notes' with brief notes for the reviewer and for Navin: what this unit is about, the key questions a teacher must answer about it, the main decisions you made with a one-line reason each, and anything uncertain. Keep the notes short; they explain the work, they are not the work.
[G-05] Never drop or compress away what the book teaches to fit a length. If a unit of work is too large, it is split by BIE into smaller units; within a unit, the book's content is complete. Lesson narration has a time target (S2-01), met by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-06] BIE is the link between the learner and the book, like a teacher (Navin, 24 October 2026). The book is the base; BIE carries its text, easy or hard, into the learner's mind. Never just read the line out: every book line is opened (what its words mean, why it is so, where it is seen, what follows), at the depth of the level profile.
[G-07] Two layers, like a film (Navin, 24 October 2026). The writer layer (understanding, plan, script) decides what is said and how deep, following the level profile and the book's own level. The presentation layer (director, video blocks, render) is the same skilled quality for every learner, from class 6 to postgraduate; only the detail shown follows the level, never the craft.
[S1-01] Read the page with two eyes: the native text blocks (exact words and numbers) and the page image (tables, diagrams, labels, arrows, equations, layout). Items that exist only in the image are as important as text items. A page whose text layer is empty or nearly empty is read entirely from the image.
[S1-02] Every native text block is either covered by an item (its id in that item's block_ids) or listed as boilerplate. Boilerplate is only running headers, page numbers, publisher adverts, contact lines and watermarks; nothing teachable is boilerplate.
[S1-03] Every table becomes one 'table' item plus one 'table_row' item per row, in order, each row's content giving every cell with its column header, for example 'Smooth muscle | Location: G.I. tract, uterus, eye, blood vessels | Function: peristalsis, blood pressure, pupil size, erects hairs | Appearance: no striations, one central nucleus | Control: involuntary'. A table continued from the previous page continues the same table.
[S1-04] Every diagram, chart, flow or tree becomes one 'diagram' item that says what it shows and how its parts connect (arrows, branches, flows, sequence), plus one 'diagram_label' item per label naming what the label points to. A classification tree lists every branch and leaf with its parent.
[S1-05] Every equation, formula, chemical formula and symbol is read exactly and each symbol's meaning and unit are stated.
[S1-06] Understand every teachable item by questioning it like a teacher. Ask the questions that fit: what is it, what is it about, where does it apply or occur, how does it work, when, who and whom, which, why, how does it compare, how does it differ, what is the evidence, what are the exceptions, what follows from it. Then keep asking 'why' and 'how' on your own answers (depth 2, 3 ...) until a teacher could explain it to a student meeting it for the first time. Answers explain; they never just repeat the item's words.
[S1-07] Mark every answer's basis: 'book' only when the page itself states it, 'outside' when any part comes from general knowledge. Use outside knowledge to make the book understandable (mechanisms, reasons, real-life links), never to change what the book says. Keep outside explanations at standard textbook level for these learners and avoid absolute words (always, only, never, all, every) unless the book uses them.
[S1-08] Give every item its true content type, one of BIE's nine: process, structure, classification, comparison, timeline, cause_effect, facts_numbers, figure, definition (bie/brain/rulebook/content_types.json). An example takes the type of what it illustrates; a question or an answer option is a role, not a type. BIE's code proposes a type before you read the page; when you choose another, say why. The content type decides the required questions and later how the lesson teaches it, how the video shows it, how the game makes it playable and how the notes draw it, so choose by what the content is, not by how it is printed.
[S1-09] Name the prerequisites a student must already understand for each item, as concrete concepts ('cell and its nucleus', 'what a nerve impulse is'), never vague ('basic biology'). Prerequisites are taught later, not just listed.
[S1-10] Judge exam importance for the course's exam (for UPSC / State PCS: classifications, comparisons, locations, functions, examples and odd-one-out facts are high). Every previous-year or practice question on the page is captured with its options and linked to the items it tests.
[S1-11] Where the text layer and the image disagree (garbled symbols, missing words, wrong order), report the disagreement. Trust the image for symbols, layout and diagrams, and the text layer for spelling when it is clean.
[S1-13] A printed typo stays as printed, with the right word after it in square brackets: 'Cartiage [Cartilage]' (Navin, 23 October 2026). The teacher answers use the right word. Never correct the book silently.
[S1-14] One answer, one basis (Navin, 23 October 2026): an answer that would mix what the book says with an outside explanation becomes two answers, one with basis 'book' (only what the page states) and one with basis 'outside'.
[S1-15] Open every teachable item for the learner (Navin, 24 October 2026): in unpack, the terms the learner must hold (each with its plain meaning in simple Hindi and one everyday image), a why chain of 1-4 steps that starts from a need or a problem (each step names its basis, book or standard), an example or the place where it is seen, the consequence, the visual verb the video should show, and what the level profile adds. Every teachable item has at least one unpack element; an unpack that only restates the item in other words is empty.

BIE's content types (the type of an item decides its required questions and how it is taught, shown, played and drawn):
- process · Process: Something that happens in steps or stages over time: a mechanism, a procedure, a cycle (photosynthesis, cell division, how a bill becomes law). Required questions: how (kaise), when (kab). Other questions: what (kya), where (kahan), why (kyun), consequence (nateeja).
- structure · Structure: Something made of parts arranged in space, each part with a function (a cell, a leaf, the heart, a machine, the Parliament). Required questions: what (kya), where (kahan). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun), which (kaun).
- classification · Classification: A group divided into kinds by a stated basis (types of tissues, kinds of rocks, kinds of writs). Required questions: which (kaun), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot), where (kahan).
- comparison · Comparison: Two or more things set side by side on stated criteria (plant and animal cells, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha). Required questions: compare (tulna), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), why (kyun), evidence (saboot).
- timeline · Timeline: Events placed in time: history, the development of an idea, stages of a life (the Revolt of 1857, evolution of cell theory). Required questions: when (kab), why (kyun). Other questions: who (kaun), where (kahan), consequence (nateeja).
- cause_effect · Reasoning (cause and effect): Why something happens: causes, effects, conditions and chains of reasoning (why tissues specialise, why prices rise, why a law was needed). Required questions: why (kyun), how (kaise). Other questions: consequence (nateeja), evidence (saboot), exception (tulna).
- facts_numbers · Facts and numbers: Stated facts, quantities, measurements, statistics and formulas (heart rate 72 per minute, 3,000 against 50,000 soldiers at Plassey, F = ma). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: compare (tulna), why (kyun).
- figure · Figure: A diagram, photo, map, graph or table drawing on the page whose content is visual (tissue pages 2, 7 and 8 are figures only). Required questions: what (kya), which (kaun). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun).
- definition · Definition: A term and its meaning as the book states it (tissue, meristem, sovereignty). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: about (kya), why (kyun).

How BIE talks to you: every request is a task card (JSON) followed by its source. The card names the unit, its parts with their content type and required questions, the ids of the rules above that apply, the output, the ids you must cover and the context. The card is BIE's instruction; the source is the material.
For a read_page card:
- card.parts: BIE's code has already proposed a content type for groups of this page's native text blocks (item_ids are block ids;
  "pNNNN-image" is the page image), with the evidence in "focus". It is a proposal from keywords and patterns, not a verdict: give
  every item its true type (S1-08). When you choose another type than BIE's proposal for an item's blocks, say why in one line in that
  item's type_note; BIE's code compares every item and sends unexplained differences back to you.
- card.coverage: every id in must_cover must be in some item's block_ids or in boilerplate_block_ids; may_skip lists blocks BIE thinks are
  running headers or page numbers. Never list an id that is not on this page.
- card.context.before and after: one line from the previous and the next page, for context only.
How to fill the JSON:
- notes: brief notes for the reviewer: what the page is about and how it fits the chapter, the key questions a teacher must answer,
  your main decisions (how you split items, how you read an unclear part, a type you chose against BIE's proposal) with a reason each,
  and what is uncertain.
- items: everything on the page, in reading order.
  - item_id: short and unique on this page ("i1", "i2", ...).
  - kind: heading, paragraph, definition, list_point, example, table (the whole table), table_row (one per row), diagram (the whole figure),
    diagram_label (one per label), equation, symbol, box_note, caption, question (a PYQ or practice question), answer_option, other.
  - parent_item_id: the table of a table_row, the diagram of a diagram_label, the question of an answer_option, else "". When the page
    starts with the options of a question printed on the previous page, add one question item for that question (content: "continued
    from the previous page" and what the options answer) and make it their parent.
  - source: "text" if the item comes from native text blocks, "image" if it is visible only in the image, "both" if both show it.
  - block_ids: the ids of the native text blocks this item covers ([] for image-only items). Use only ids from the card.
  - where_on_page: where it is ("top table, row 2", "right diagram, label at the axon end").
  - content: the exact words for text items; a complete, faithful reading for image items (every cell with its column header for a
    table_row; what a label names and what it points to for a diagram_label; all branches for a tree). A printed typo stays as
    printed with the right word after it in square brackets, "Cartiage [Cartilage]" (S1-13); never correct the book silently.
  - content_type: one of BIE's nine type ids above, by what the content is. An example takes the type of what it illustrates; a table
    row or a diagram label usually takes its table's or diagram's type. "none" only for a question, an answer option or an item that is
    not teachable.
  - type_note: "" when you agree with BIE's proposal for this item's blocks (or there is none); otherwise one line on why your type fits.
  - teachable: false only for pure headings and containers whose children carry the content.
  - teacher_understanding: the teacher's questions and answers for this item (S1-06); depth 1 for first questions, 2 and more for
    "why"/"how" on an earlier answer; basis "book" only if the page states it, else "outside"; one answer, one basis: an answer that
    would mix what the book says with an outside explanation becomes two answers, one "book" and one "outside" (S1-14). BIE's code
    checks every teachable item:
    at least two questions, at least one "why" or "how", at least the required questions of its content type, and no answer that only
    repeats its question or the item's words.
  - prerequisites: concrete concepts a student must understand first.
  - exam_importance and exam_note: for this exam.
  - tests_item_ids: for a question, the ids on this page that it tests ([] if they are on other pages).
  - unpack: how a teacher opens this book line for the learner (S1-15; BIE is the link between the learner and the book, never a
    reader of the line). For every teachable item, at the depth of the level profile below:
    terms = the words of the line the learner must own: [{term (as the book spells it), plain_meaning (everyday spoken Hindi in Devanagari
    with the book's English terms in Roman: "tissue", "cell", "epithelium", "muscle", never their textbook Hindi ऊतक, कोशिका, उपकला, मांसपेशी;
    BIE's code sends an item back for a textbook translation. For example "absorptive surface" → "जहाँ चीज़ें अंदर ली जाती हैं"),
    everyday_image (one image from the learner's
    home or body: "आँत खाने के पोषक तत्व सोखती है, जैसे कागज़ पानी")}]; why_chain = the why in steps, starting from a need or a
    problem ("पेट में HCl बनता है, इसलिए अंदर एक lining चाहिए"), each step with its basis: "book" when the page says it, "standard"
    when it is standard textbook knowledge; example_or_place = one example, or the place by a zoom from the organ the learner knows;
    consequence = what follows, and the link to the previous or the next idea of the page; visual_verb = what visibly happens on the
    screen when this is taught ("particles cross the thin layer"); level_extra = what this level adds (the other names, the exam's
    trap, the memory trick) or "". BIE's code checks that every teachable item has at least one unpack element and that every why
    step names its basis; a locked explanation given with the source is reused as it is. A question item or a pure heading leaves
    unpack empty.
- boilerplate_block_ids: ids of running headers, page numbers, adverts, contact lines and watermarks only.
- text_image_disagreements: where the text layer and the image differ.
Reply with the JSON object only.

Level profile: UPSC / State PCS (level_profiles.json; learners: UPSC and State PCS aspirants, often from arts backgrounds, who need understanding more than technical vocabulary).
- Terms: fewer technical terms: only the ones the exam asks, each opened with its plain meaning and an everyday image; a term the exam never asks is explained in words, not named.
- Why: 2 step(s); a two-step why from a need the learner can feel, then its link to daily life, health or governance.
- Where found: the main places, each linked to something the learner already knows (a disease, a food, a news item).
- Exam beats: the PYQ pattern: how this fact has been asked (statement combinations, 'which is correct', odd one out) and the wording that traps.
- Links: daily life, health, the news and earlier chapters of the same paper.

How real teachers open a book line (teacher example bank 2026-10-24.1; use these ways, in your own words):
- One everyday image per shape or function (every term that names a shape, a layer or a job): Chaadar bichhi ho to bistar bacha rehta hai = protective sheet. Cube wala game, har side barabar = cuboidal. Building ka pillar = columnar. Farsh ki tiles = squamous, isliye tessellated bhi kehte hain.
- The word root where it helps (a term whose parts carry its meaning): Epi yaani upar; epithelium yaani upar ki parat. Slender yaani long aur narrow.
- Why starts from a need (every why step): Pet mein HCl banta hai, isliye andar ek lining chahiye jo khud na jale. Cells bahar ki taraf hain, tootne ka chance zyada, isliye regeneration zyada.
- Link to something already known (a new place or a new structure): Peritoneum, jaise lungs ke aas-paas pleura aur heart ke aas-paas pericardium: wahi kaam, pet ke andar.
- Meaning with two or three real examples (an abstract word in the book): Sensory perception yaani pehchanna: thanda lagna, dard hona, pressure mehsoos karna.
- Open the book's adjective (Navin's example) (a book line names a kind of surface, job or place without saying what it is): Book: 'epithelium absorptive aur secretive surfaces par milta hai'. Teacher: absorptive surface yaani jahan cheezein andar li jaati hain, jaise aant khane ke poshak tatva sokhti hai; secretive yaani jahan cells kuch bana kar bahar chhodte hain, jaise glands enzyme ya juice. Aur epithelium wahan kyon? Kyunki ek patli, lagi hui parat hi cheezon ko paar jaane de sakti hai aur bana kar chhod sakti hai.

p0018-b0001 | Indian Economy
p0018-b0002 | • In an economy, money circulates continuously between households, businesses, banks, and
p0018-b0003 | the RBI.
p0018-b0004 | • M0: M0 is the money created directly by the RBI.
p0018-b0005 | o It is called Reserve Money or High-Powered Money because it forms the base from
p0018-b0006 | which banks create additional money through lending.
p0018-b0007 | • M0 = C + OD + Bankers Deposits
p0018-b0008 | o C = Currency in circulation
p0018-b0009 | o OD = Other deposits with RBI
p0018-b0010 | o Bankers' Deposits = Commercial banks' deposits with RBI (including CRR balances)
p0018-b0011 | • When banks receive reserves from the RBI, they can lend multiple times, expanding the
p0018-b0012 | money supply.
p0018-b0013 | • M1 – Narrow Money
p0018-b0014 | o M1 is the most liquid money available to the public for everyday transactions.
p0018-b0015 | • M1= Currency + Demand Deposits + Other Deposits with RBI
p0018-b0016 | • It includes:
p0018-b0017 | o Currency with the public
p0018-b0018 | o Demand deposits (current and savings accounts that can be withdrawn on demand)
p0018-b0019 | o Other deposits with RBI
p0018-b0020 | • It is called Narrow Money because every component can be spent almost immediately.
p0018-b0021 | • M2 – Intermediate Money
p0018-b0022 | o M2 is a broader measure than M1.
p0018-b0023 | • M2 = M1 + Savings Deposits with Post Office Savings Banks.
p0018-b0024 | • It adds post office Savings Bank deposits (excluding National Savings Certificates and

output.page_summary: M0 is RBI-created reserve money. M1 comprises immediately usable money; M2 adds post-office savings deposits, excluding NSCs and similar instruments; M3 adds bank time deposits to M1 and is the principal money-supply measure discussed. RBI monitors M3 for inflationary pressure, liquidity, credit growth and monetary-policy effectiveness. M4 is introduced as the broadest measure.

items.content: In an economy, money circulates continuously between households, businesses, banks, and the RBI.

teacher_understanding.question: Between which participants does money circulate?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page connects households, businesses, banks and the RBI rather than treating money as something held by one group.

teacher_understanding.question: When does this circulation occur?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page describes it as continuous, not confined to a single issue of currency by the RBI.

teacher_understanding.question: How can a learner picture this circulation in daily life?
teacher_understanding.answer: A household pays a shop, the shop deposits receipts in a bank, and the bank handles payments and lending. Banks also maintain balances and settle transactions through the RBI. These are different links, not a requirement that each payment pass through every participant.

prerequisites: Money as a means of payment
items.exam_note: Provides the setting for distinguishing RBI money from bank deposits.

terms.plain_meaning: पैसा भुगतान और जमा के साथ एक से दूसरे के पास जाता रहता है
terms.everyday_image: घर से दुकान तक payment, फिर दुकान की कमाई bank में

why_chain.step: People need to buy goods, receive income and store balances, so money changes hands.
The page places households, businesses, banks and the RBI within this continuing circulation.

unpack.example_or_place: A salary credited to a bank account and subsequently spent at a shop.
unpack.consequence: Understanding different holders prepares the learner to distinguish reserves from public money holdings.
unpack.visual_verb: Move payment tokens between named participants.
unpack.level_extra: Do not confuse circulation of existing money with creation of additional money.

items.content:
M0: M0 is the money created directly by the RBI.
It is called Reserve Money or High-Powered Money because it forms the base from which banks create additional money through lending.

teacher_understanding.question: What is M0, and what other names does it have?
teacher_understanding.answer: M0 identifies money directly created by the RBI; Reserve Money and High-Powered Money name the same base-money concept here.

teacher_understanding.question: What feature on the page explains the name High-Powered Money?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page says it forms the base from which banks create additional money through lending.

teacher_understanding.question: Why distinguish this base from deposits created by commercial banks?
teacher_understanding.answer: Commercial-bank deposit balances can expand when banks grant loans, but those balances are not themselves newly issued RBI reserve balances. Separating the two prevents counting all bank money as directly created by the RBI.

items.exam_note: Test synonyms and the distinction between reserve money and broad money.

terms.plain_meaning: RBI से बना वह आधार पैसा जिस पर banks का आगे का money creation टिका है
terms.everyday_image: इमारत की नींव और उसके ऊपर बनी मंज़िलें

terms.plain_meaning: उसी base money का नाम, जिससे आगे bank deposits बढ़ने का आधार मिलता है
terms.everyday_image: एक आधार से कई ऊपर की परतों को सहारा

why_chain.step: Banks need a foundation of central-bank money for cash needs and settlement.
The page calls this lending-supporting base Reserve Money or High-Powered Money.

unpack.example_or_place: A commercial bank's balance held at the RBI.
unpack.consequence: M0 must be separated from the public's spendable deposits in M1.
unpack.visual_verb: Build deposit layers above a labelled M0 foundation.
unpack.level_extra: The three labels M0, Reserve Money and High-Powered Money refer to the same aggregate in this discussion.

items.where_on_page: upper section, M0 formula and three indented definitions
items.content:
M0 = C + OD + Bankers Deposits
C = Currency in circulation
OD = Other deposits with RBI
Bankers' Deposits = Commercial banks' deposits with RBI (including CRR balances)

teacher_understanding.question: What does each term in the M0 equation represent?
teacher_understanding.answer: M0 is reserve money; C is currency in circulation; OD is other deposits with the RBI; Bankers' Deposits are commercial banks' deposits with the RBI, including CRR balances. The plus signs add these monetary amounts, and the equals sign identifies their total as M0.

teacher_understanding.question: What explicitly establishes that CRR balances belong in M0?
teacher_understanding.answer: The component definition includes CRR balances within commercial banks' deposits with the RBI.

teacher_understanding.question: How should these quantities be measured and added?
teacher_understanding.answer: They are stocks of money measured at a common date in a common monetary unit, such as rupees or crore rupees. The page specifies no particular unit or numerical values. M0 is an aggregate label, not money raised to the power zero.

teacher_understanding.question: How do currency in circulation and currency with the public differ?
teacher_understanding.answer: Currency in circulation includes bank-held cash as well as currency held by the public. Currency with the public excludes banks' cash holdings. This matters when moving from the M0 formula to M1.

teacher_understanding.question: What does CRR mean in this context?
teacher_understanding.answer: CRR is the Cash Reserve Ratio: a required proportion of specified bank liabilities maintained as cash balances with the RBI. Those balances are bank assets at the central bank, not household savings accounts.

items.exam_note: Component-identification trap: banks' balances at RBI enter M0; customers' bank deposits are different. Do not equate C here with currency with the public.

terms.plain_meaning: चलन में मौजूद cash, जिसमें public और banks के पास का cash शामिल है
terms.everyday_image: जेब के नोट और bank के cash counter के नोट

terms.plain_meaning: commercial banks का RBI में रखा balance
terms.everyday_image: आपका account bank में; bank का balance RBI में

terms.plain_meaning: नियम के मुताबिक banks को RBI में जो cash balance रखना पड़ता है
terms.everyday_image: कमाई का तय हिस्सा अलग रखने वाला डिब्बा

terms.plain_meaning: इस formula में RBI के पास Other deposits
terms.everyday_image: RBI की सूची में banks के balance से अलग एक deposit खांचा

why_chain.step: To measure RBI-created money, cash alone is insufficient because RBI deposit balances also matter.
The formula therefore adds currency, other RBI deposits and bankers' RBI deposits.

unpack.example_or_place: Compare a bank's RBI account with a household's savings account at that bank.
unpack.consequence: The location and holder of a deposit determine its role in an aggregate.
unpack.visual_verb: Combine three labelled amounts into M0 and highlight CRR inside bankers' deposits.
unpack.level_extra: OD means Other deposits here, not overdraft; use the page's definition. No numerical multiplier is provided.

items.content: When banks receive reserves from the RBI, they can lend multiple times, expanding the money supply.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the page link RBI reserves to the money supply?
teacher_understanding.answer: It presents reserves received from the RBI as a base supporting bank lending and expansion of money supply.

teacher_understanding.question: When does the reserve-supported expansion described here become possible?
teacher_understanding.answer: The stated starting condition is banks receiving reserves from the RBI.

teacher_understanding.question: How can lending create money beyond the initial reserve base?
teacher_understanding.answer: A bank loan normally creates a matching borrower deposit. Spending moves that deposit through the banking system, and reserves help banks settle resulting payments. Further lending can expand deposits across the system.

teacher_understanding.question: Does 'lend multiple times' imply unlimited lending or a fixed automatic multiplier?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. Reserve and cash needs, capital rules, borrower demand and credit risk constrain lending. Expansion depends on conditions; the sentence should not be read as one bank repeatedly lending the same cash without limits.

items.exam_note: Understand deposit creation while rejecting claims of unlimited or mechanically guaranteed lending.

terms.plain_meaning: banks के पास payment और cash की जरूरत सँभालने वाला आधार balance
terms.everyday_image: दुकान के रोज़ के लेन-देन के लिए रखा cash

why_chain.step: Borrowers need spending balances, and banks need to settle payments arising from loans.
Reserve-supported lending can expand bank deposits and hence money supply, subject to constraints.

unpack.example_or_place: A loan credited to an account is used to pay a seller who banks elsewhere.
unpack.consequence: Explains why reserve money and money-supply aggregates need not be equal.
unpack.visual_verb: Credit a loan deposit, transfer it to a seller, and settle between banks.
unpack.level_extra: Distinguish a system-wide expansion mechanism from unlimited lending by an individual bank.

items.content:
M1 – Narrow Money
M1 is the most liquid money available to the public for everyday transactions.

teacher_understanding.question: What does M1 measure in this introduction?
teacher_understanding.answer: It focuses on the public's most readily usable money for routine payments, under the name Narrow Money.

teacher_understanding.question: What phrase establishes the liquidity focus of M1?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page calls it the 'most liquid money' available for everyday transactions.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does liquidity matter for an everyday payment?
teacher_understanding.answer: A balance is more liquid when it can be used quickly with little difficulty or loss of value. Shopping requires a usable payment balance, not merely an asset that may take time to turn into spending money.

items.exam_note: Associate M1 with Narrow Money and immediate transaction use, not all financial wealth.

terms.plain_meaning: जिसे जल्दी और आसानी से payment में लगा सकें
terms.everyday_image: दूध खरीदने के लिए जेब का cash, मकान बेचने की जरूरत नहीं

terms.plain_meaning: तुरंत खर्च होने वाले हिस्सों पर केंद्रित money का माप
terms.everyday_image: पूरी संपत्ति की जगह रोज़ के खर्च वाला बटुआ

why_chain.step: Daily purchases require payment resources that are readily accessible.
M1 focuses on the most liquid money available to the public.

unpack.example_or_place: Cash and a usable balance in an ordinary transaction account.
unpack.consequence: Liquidity provides the reason for grouping the following M1 components.
unpack.visual_verb: Select readily spendable balances from a wider asset collection.
unpack.level_extra: Liquidity describes ease of use, not a high rate of interest.

items.where_on_page: middle, M1 equation and inclusion list
items.content:
M1= Currency + Demand Deposits + Other Deposits with RBI
It includes:
Currency with the public
Demand deposits (current and savings accounts that can be withdrawn on demand)
Other deposits with RBI

teacher_understanding.question: What enters M1, and what does 'Currency' mean here?
teacher_understanding.answer: The accompanying list identifies currency as currency with the public. M1 adds it to demand deposits and other deposits with the RBI. The page describes current and savings accounts withdrawable on demand as demand deposits.

teacher_understanding.question: What in the page resolves the short formula's wording?
teacher_understanding.answer: The list immediately below the formula explicitly says 'Currency with the public' and explains demand deposits through current and savings accounts.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the demand feature make a deposit suitable for M1?
teacher_understanding.answer: The depositor need not wait for an agreed maturity before requesting withdrawal or making permitted payments. That access distinguishes a demand balance from a time deposit.

teacher_understanding.question: Why should banks' RBI balances not be substituted for public demand deposits?
teacher_understanding.answer: Banks' RBI balances are held by banks at the central bank; public demand deposits are liabilities of commercial banks to their customers. They occupy different layers of the monetary system.

teacher_understanding.question: What units and notation apply to the M1 equation?
teacher_understanding.answer: M1 is the name of an aggregate, not a power. Its components are monetary stocks added in a common unit at a common date; the page gives no numerical unit or amounts.

items.exam_note: Statement-combination traps include inserting time deposits or bankers' RBI deposits into the M1 component list.

terms.plain_meaning: ऐसा account balance जिसे मांगने पर निकाल सकें, तय maturity का इंतज़ार नहीं
terms.everyday_image: ज़रूरत पर savings account से पैसे निकालना

terms.plain_meaning: public के पास मौजूद cash; banks के पास का cash नहीं
terms.everyday_image: घर की दराज़ और लोगों के बटुओं के नोट

why_chain.step: A transaction-money measure needs balances accessible for current payments.
The page combines public currency, demand deposits and other RBI deposits in M1.

unpack.example_or_place: A household's cash and withdrawable savings-account balance illustrate two listed components.
unpack.consequence: M1 becomes the common starting aggregate for both M2 and M3 on this page.
unpack.visual_verb: Add three labelled component boxes into M1.
unpack.level_extra: Read the formula together with its list: Currency here is not the full currency-in-circulation term used for M0.

items.content: It is called Narrow Money because every component can be spent almost immediately.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the adjective Narrow emphasise here?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page limits attention to components available for spending almost immediately rather than the wider range of deposit balances.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the page's stated reason for the name?
teacher_understanding.answer: It explicitly links the name to the near-immediate spendability of every included component.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does this help distinguish narrow from broad money?
teacher_understanding.answer: Broader measures can add balances that are money-like but less immediately available. 'Narrow' describes coverage, not the physical size of notes or the amount of money held by a person.

items.exam_note: Retain 'almost immediately'; avoid interpreting liquidity as an absence of any transaction rules.

terms.plain_meaning: खर्च के लिए आम तौर पर लंबा इंतज़ार नहीं करना पड़ता
terms.everyday_image: आज की खरीद के लिए आज ही account का पैसा इस्तेमाल करना

why_chain.step: A learner needs to separate current spending capacity from balances tied up for later.
The page explains Narrow Money through near-immediate spendability.

unpack.example_or_place: Compare a readily usable savings balance with money placed in a fixed deposit.
unpack.consequence: The next aggregates broaden coverage beyond this immediate-payment core.
unpack.visual_verb: Highlight a readily spendable inner set.
unpack.level_extra: Narrow versus broad refers to included components, not denominations.

items.content:
M2 – Intermediate Money
M2 is a broader measure than M1.

teacher_understanding.question: How does M2 compare with M1 in coverage?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page names M2 Intermediate Money and gives it wider coverage than M1.

teacher_understanding.question: What addition accounts for that wider coverage?
teacher_understanding.answer: The following formula adds savings deposits with Post Office Savings Banks to M1.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does broader not mean more liquid?
teacher_understanding.answer: Coverage expands when an additional category is included, even if that category is less convenient for payments. Size of the covered set and ease of spending are different criteria.

prerequisites: Meaning of including an additional component
items.exam_note: Broader coverage must not be confused with higher liquidity.

terms.plain_meaning: पहले वाले माप से ज़्यादा तरह के balances को गिनने वाला माप
terms.everyday_image: छोटे घेरे के बाहर एक और हिस्सा जोड़ना

why_chain.step: Measuring only immediate transaction balances leaves out some accessible savings.
M2 broadens M1 by adding post-office savings deposits.

unpack.example_or_place: The savings account held at a post office rather than an ordinary bank.
unpack.consequence: The next equation identifies the precise added component.
unpack.visual_verb: Extend the M1 set with a post-office savings section.
unpack.level_extra: Recognise Intermediate Money as the page's label for M2.

items.content:
M2 = M1 + Savings Deposits with Post Office Savings Banks.
It adds post office Savings Bank deposits (excluding National Savings Certificates and similar instruments).
items.type_note: The 'similar instruments' phrase specifies an exclusion from a formula component; it does not compare two measures.

teacher_understanding.question: What exactly is added to M1 to obtain M2?
teacher_understanding.answer: Savings deposits with Post Office Savings Banks are added. The page explicitly excludes National Savings Certificates and similar instruments from that addition.

teacher_understanding.question: What prevents interpreting M2 as including every post-office savings product?
teacher_understanding.answer: The parenthetical exclusion names National Savings Certificates and similar instruments.

teacher_understanding.question: Why distinguish an account deposit from a savings certificate?
teacher_understanding.answer: Products sold at the same institution can have different withdrawal and maturity arrangements. The post-office location alone does not make every product a savings-account deposit.

teacher_understanding.question: How should the notation and units be read?
teacher_understanding.answer: M2 names the aggregate. Add the M1 stock and eligible post-office savings-deposit stock in the same monetary unit and at the same date. The page supplies no numerical values or specified unit.

items.exam_note: High-value exclusion: NSCs do not enter merely because they are offered by the post office.

terms.term: Savings Deposits with Post Office Savings Banks
terms.plain_meaning: post office के savings accounts में जमा balance
terms.everyday_image: post office की savings passbook में लिखा balance

terms.plain_meaning: एक savings certificate वाला product, जिसे यहाँ जोड़ने से साफ मना किया गया है
terms.everyday_image: साधारण account passbook से अलग खरीदा हुआ savings certificate

why_chain.step: To calculate the aggregate correctly, one must identify the eligible product rather than just its selling institution.
The page includes post-office savings deposits but excludes NSCs and similar instruments.

unpack.example_or_place: At a post-office counter, distinguish a savings-account deposit from a savings-certificate purchase.
unpack.consequence: The exclusion controls which balances may be added to M1.
unpack.visual_verb: Add a savings-account box and cross out a certificate box.
unpack.level_extra: A statement saying 'all post-office savings instruments enter M2' conflicts with this page.

items.content: These deposits are fairly liquid but slightly less convenient than ordinary bank deposits.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the page compare post-office savings deposits with ordinary bank deposits?
teacher_understanding.answer: It describes the post-office deposits as fairly liquid while giving ordinary bank deposits an advantage in convenience.

teacher_understanding.question: Does the page describe these deposits as illiquid?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. It retains the description 'fairly liquid'; the qualification concerns their slightly lower convenience.

teacher_understanding.question: How can liquidity and convenience differ?
teacher_understanding.answer: A balance may be withdrawable but require an extra step before a particular payment. Payment access and withdrawal arrangements affect convenience without making the balance wholly inaccessible. The page specifies no particular operational restriction.

items.exam_note: Do not turn 'slightly less convenient' into 'cannot be withdrawn' or a universal claim about present-day payment facilities.

terms.plain_meaning: काफी आसानी से पैसा मिल सकता है, पर payment में थोड़ी कम सहूलियत हो सकती है
terms.everyday_image: पैसा मौजूद है, लेकिन खरीद से पहले एक और काम करना पड़ सकता है

why_chain.step: People need both access to savings and convenient ways to make payments.
The page treats post-office savings as fairly liquid but slightly less convenient than ordinary bank deposits.

unpack.example_or_place: Comparing the steps needed to use two different savings accounts for a purchase.
unpack.consequence: Explains why broader coverage need not imply greater immediate transaction convenience.
unpack.visual_verb: Compare two payment paths with different numbers of steps.
unpack.level_extra: This is the book's qualitative comparison, not a detailed current-services comparison.

items.content:
M3 – Broad Money
It is the most important money supply measure in India.
When newspapers report money supply growth, they usually mean M3.

teacher_understanding.question: What importance does the page assign to M3?
teacher_understanding.answer: It names M3 Broad Money and presents it as India's most important money-supply measure.

teacher_understanding.question: What practical reporting context does the page give for M3?
teacher_understanding.answer: It says newspaper reports of money-supply growth usually refer to M3.

teacher_understanding.question: Why can a wider deposit-based measure be useful in economic reporting?
teacher_understanding.answer: It captures a wider range of monetary holdings than immediate transaction balances alone, helping discussions of liquidity and financing conditions go beyond cash in people's wallets.

items.exam_note: M3 is Broad Money and the principal measure here; M4, not M3, is described as broadest. Preserve 'usually' in the reporting claim.

terms.plain_meaning: तुरंत खर्च वाले पैसे के साथ कुछ और bank deposits को भी गिनने वाला माप
terms.everyday_image: रोज़ के खर्च वाले खाते के साथ FD का balance भी देखना

why_chain.step: Economic reporting needs a picture wider than cash and immediately usable balances.
The page identifies M3 as the most important measure and the usual newspaper reference.

unpack.example_or_place: A newspaper headline on money-supply growth.
unpack.consequence: The next formula shows which extra bank deposits make M3 broad.
unpack.visual_verb: Link a money-supply headline to the M3 label.
unpack.level_extra: Most important does not mean broadest; do not replace 'usually' with 'always'.

items.where_on_page: lower section, M3 formula and deposit list
items.content:
M3 = M1 + Time Deposits with Banks
It includes:
Everything in M1
Fixed deposits
Recurring deposits
Other time deposits with commercial banks

teacher_understanding.question: What is the composition of M3 on this page?
teacher_understanding.answer: M3 includes the entire M1 aggregate plus bank time deposits. The listed time-deposit categories are fixed deposits, recurring deposits and other time deposits with commercial banks.

teacher_understanding.question: What confirms that M3 does not replace the components of M1?
teacher_understanding.answer: Both the equation's addition of M1 and the phrase 'Everything in M1' show that the existing M1 components are retained.

teacher_understanding.question: How do time deposits differ from demand deposits?
teacher_understanding.answer: Time deposits are arranged for an agreed period rather than being designed primarily as balances payable on demand. Early access can be subject to conditions or penalties, so their inclusion broadens money beyond the most immediate payment balances.

teacher_understanding.question: How do fixed and recurring deposits illustrate time deposits?
teacher_understanding.answer: A fixed deposit generally places a sum for an agreed term; a recurring deposit accumulates scheduled instalments under a term arrangement. Both differ from simply keeping an unrestricted transaction balance.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the crucial formula difference between M2 and M3?
teacher_understanding.answer: M2 adds post-office savings deposits to M1; M3 adds time deposits with banks to M1. The printed M3 equation does not start from M2.

teacher_understanding.question: What units and notation apply to M3?
teacher_understanding.answer: M3 is an aggregate label. M1 and bank time deposits must be measured as stocks at the same date in a common monetary unit. The page gives no amounts or unit.

items.exam_note: Common formula trap: M3 = M1 + bank time deposits, not M2 + bank time deposits. Recognise both FD and RD in the listed coverage.

terms.plain_meaning: तय समय की शर्त के साथ bank में जमा पैसा
terms.everyday_image: एक तय तारीख तक रखी गई FD

terms.plain_meaning: एक रकम को तय समय के लिए जमा रखना

items.content:
The RBI watches M3 because it helps indicate:
Inflationary pressures
Liquidity in the economy
Credit growth
Effectiveness of monetary policy

teacher_understanding.question: Why does the RBI monitor M3?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page links M3 monitoring to four indications: inflationary pressures, liquidity in the economy, credit growth and effectiveness of monetary policy.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the page characterise the information M3 provides?
teacher_understanding.answer: It says M3 'helps indicate' these conditions; it presents M3 as informative rather than giving a numerical rule or claiming that it alone determines them.

teacher_understanding.question: How can M3 relate to inflationary pressures?
teacher_understanding.answer: If expanding money holdings support spending faster than production can respond, pressure on prices can increase. The relationship also depends on output, willingness to spend and other conditions, so M3 growth alone does not establish inflation.

teacher_understanding.question: How can M3 indicate liquidity in the economy?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its currency and deposit components help show the scale and evolution of monetary balances. Because time deposits are included, the whole total should not be interpreted as immediately spendable cash.

teacher_understanding.question: How can M3 be linked to credit growth?
teacher_understanding.answer: Bank lending commonly creates deposits, so changes in deposit-based money can accompany credit expansion. Deposits and credit are different measures, however, and need not grow one-for-one.

teacher_understanding.question: How can M3 help assess monetary-policy effectiveness?
teacher_understanding.answer: Policy changes can affect funding, lending and deposit growth. Observing M3 alongside other indicators helps assess whether financial conditions are responding in the intended direction; M3 alone cannot prove success.

items.exam_note: Learn all four monitoring purposes. Reject statements that M3 alone mechanically determines inflation or equals bank credit.

items.content:
M4:
It is the broadest measure of money supply in India.

teacher_understanding.question: What does this page establish about M4?
teacher_understanding.answer: It identifies M4 as the broadest money-supply measure in India, without giving its component formula here.

teacher_understanding.question: What distinguishes M4's description from M3's?
teacher_understanding.answer: M4 is called 'broadest', whereas M3 is called the 'most important' measure and the usual reference in newspaper reporting.

teacher_understanding.question: Why can the broadest measure differ from the most important reporting measure?
teacher_understanding.answer: Breadth concerns the range of included components; reporting importance concerns analytical and practical use. A measure need not have the widest coverage to be the principal reference.

items.exam_note: Distinguish M3 as the most important measure from M4 as the broadest. Do not infer a formula from this page.
